blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning for language models has moved from preference reward models to verifiable rewards, which sustain much longer optimization. Preference models are prone to reward hacking: the policy raises their score without improving response quality, or even while degrading it. Yet for open-ended tasks, where quality can neither be verified nor fully written down as rubrics, they remain valuable. We introduce Dynalize, which mitigates reward hacking online, during policy training. Periodically and asynchronously, a language model analyzes training rollouts and writes penalties for undesirable behaviors that the reward model appears to reward; a judge applies them to every rollout. In clinical counseling and creative writing, training on the reward model alone raises its score continuously but ultimately leads to a decline in external benchmarks. Dynalize sustains longer training and results in improved downstream performance. For example, we find that our method suppresses patterns incentivized by preference models that, without penalties, spread to most responses, and even to the model's reasoning, which the reward model does not explicitly score. Furthermore, we show that its gains hold in multi-turn training, and even after we retrain the reward model on the discovered behaviors.
blocks.zh: 对语言模式的强化学习已经从优惠奖励模式转向可核查的奖励,这维持了更长的优化. 偏好模式容易被奖励黑客:政策提高他们的分数而不提高反应质量,甚至贬低反应质量. 然而,对于无法核实质量或无法将质量完全记为标题的开放式任务,这些任务仍然很有价值。 我们引入了Dynalize, 它减轻奖励在线黑客, 在政策培训。 一个语言模型定期和同步地分析培训的推出,并写出奖赏模型似乎奖励的不良行为的惩罚;法官在每次推出时都应用这些方法。 在临床咨询和创造性写作方面,仅关于奖励模式的培训不断提高其分数,但最终导致外部基准下降。 Dynalize使培训持续时间更长,提高了下游的业绩。 例如,我们发现,我们的方法压制了各种模式,这些模式被优惠模式所激励,这些模式在没有惩罚的情况下传播到大多数响应,甚至到模型的推理上,而奖励模式没有明确得分. 此外,我们表明,它的收益体现在多轮培训,甚至在我们重新培训关于所发现行为的奖励模式之后。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning (RL) is emerging as the de facto paradigm for improving large language models (LLMs), and currently takes a growing share of the compute used to train them — in some cases matching or even exceeding pretraining ( Lambert, 2025 ; Karpathy, 2025 ; DeepSeek-AI and others, 2025b ; xAI, 2025 ; Cursor, 2026 ) . This scale-up derives, in part, from a shift in reward design: earlier models were mostly trained with preference models, i.e., reward models (RMs) fitted to pairwise human preferences with the Bradley-Terry model ( Bradley and Terry, 1952 ; Christiano et al., 2017 ; Ouyang et al., 2022 ) , whereas verifiable rewards, such as answer checks in mathematics or unit tests in code, are now the standard ( Lambert et al., 2024 ; DeepSeek-AI and others, 2025a ) .
blocks.zh: 加强学习正在成为改进大语言模型(LLM)的事实上的范例,目前,在用于培训大语言模型的计算中占有越来越大的份额——在某些情况下,这种计算与预培训相匹配甚至超过预培训(Lambert,2025;Karepathy,2025;Deepseek-AI等,2025b;xAI,2025;Cursor,2026). 这种扩大部分来源于奖励设计的转变:早期的模型大多以优惠模式进行训练,即奖励模式与布拉德利-特瑞模式(Bradley和Terry,1952年;Christiano等,2017年;Ouyang等,2022年)相配,而可核查的奖励,如数学中的答题检查或编码中的单位测试,现在是标准(Lambert等,2024年;DeepSeek-AI等,2025a年)。

blocks.en: Verifiable rewards allow much longer optimization ( DeepSeek-AI and others, 2025a ; Karpathy, 2025 ; xAI, 2025 ) than preference models, which are widely known to be prone to reward hacking ( Skalse et al., 2022 ; Wang et al., 2026b ) . As optimization progresses, the policy may discover and exploit shortcuts that do not reflect response adequacy and quality (e.g., lexical features or response length; Xia et al., 2025 ; Srivastava et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ), thus increasing reward-model scores without improving, or even while degrading, downstream response quality.
blocks.zh: 可核实的奖励允许比偏好模式更长时间的优化(DeepSeek-AI等,2025a;Karopathy,2025;xAI,2025),这些模式被广为人知,容易被奖励黑客(Skalse等,2022;Wang等,2026b.). 随着优化工作的进展,该政策可能发现并利用不反映响应充足性和质量的捷径(如:词汇特征或响应长度;霞等,2025;斯里瓦斯塔瓦等,2025;王等,2026b等),从而在不提高甚至降低下游响应质量的情况下提高奖励模式分数.

blocks.en: However, not all tasks, particularly open-ended ones such as clinical counseling and creative writing, can easily be put in a form that a program can verify ( Jia et al., 2025 ; Gunjal et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) . For these tasks, rubric-based rewards have emerged as an alternative to do away with preference models ( DeepSeek-AI and others, 2025b ; DeepSeek-AI and others, 2026 ) : reward scores are derived from LLM judges running each response against a predefined set of rubrics ( Gunjal et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Kimi Team, 2025 ; Kimi Team, 2026 ; Qi et al., 2026a ) (typically written for each task or instance; Huang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ). Yet a rubric rewards only what its authors — humans or language models — thought or were prompted to write down ( Mahmoud et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . 1 1 1 Rubrics are hard to set even with clinical expertise: psychiatrists agree poorly when they rate LLM responses with a shared, calibrated rubric ( Jafari Meimandi et al., 2026 ) . We argue that, for such tasks, preference models remain valuable: they can encode information that is hard to write down, and promote and penalize behaviors and properties that are hard to enumerate. And although previous work has attempted to make reward models more robust and less exploitable ( Srivastava et al., 2025 ; Bukharin et al., 2025 ; Coste et al., 2024 ; Eisenstein et al., 2024 ; Duan et al., 2026 ) , it is hard, if not impossible, to rely purely on reward models (and combinations thereof) during training and remain exploit-free.
blocks.zh: 然而,并非所有任务,特别是临床咨询和创造性写作等开放式任务,都能够轻易地以一个方案可以核实的形式(Jia等,2025;Gunjal等,2025;Huang等,2025;张等,2025;Wang等,2026a). 对于这些任务,基于卢标的奖励已经出现,作为取消优惠模式的替代(DeepSeek-AI等,2025b;DeepSeek-AI等,2026):奖励分取自LLM评委根据预先确定的一套卢标(Gunjal等,2025;Huang等,2025;Kimi Team等,2026;Qi等,2026a)(通常为每项任务或案例写出;Huang等,2026;Li等,2026)。 然而,只是给其作者——人类或语言模型——所想的或被诱使写作的奖赏而已(Mahmoud等,2026;Yang等,2026.). 1 1 1 Rubrics即使具备临床专业知识也很难设定:精神病学家在用共同的,校准的卢布来评分LLM反应时,不同意(Jafari Meimandi等,2026.). 我们主张,对于这些任务来说,偏好模式仍然很有价值:它们可以编码难以被记下来的信息,促进和惩罚难以列举的行为和财产. 虽然以前的工作试图使奖励模式更加健全和较少被利用(Srivastava等,2025年;Bukharin等,2025年;Coste等,2024年;Eisenstein等,2024年;Duan等,2026年),但在培训期间,即使不是不可能,也很难完全依靠奖励模式(及其组合),并且保持无剥削状态.

blocks.en: As such, in this work, we focus on addressing this gap by exploring methods to mitigate reward hacking of preference models online , adaptively during policy training. We introduce Dynalize , a method that complements a reward model with penalties that evolve during training. Periodically, during the RL climb, a separate language model analyzes policy rollouts and their reward scores, identifies undesirable behaviors that appear to be rewarded by the RM, and writes penalties for them. A dynamic penalty buffer keeps these penalties up to date, adding new ones and discarding those that are no longer triggered by the policy at the time. Importantly, both the proposal and the buffer update run asynchronously, without interrupting policy optimization. Finally, a judge applies the buffer’s penalties to each rollout, so the reward for gradient updates adapts to the reward-hacking patterns observed during training, while the RM still defines response quality.
blocks.zh: 因此,在这项工作中,我们侧重于解决这一差距,探讨在政策培训期间以适应性方式在线减少对优惠模式的奖励黑客行为的方法。 我们引入了Dynalize, 这种方法补充奖励模式, 周期性地,在RL攀升期间,一个单独的语言模型分析政策推出及其奖励分数,识别似乎受到RM奖励的不良行为,并写出对他们的处罚. 动态的处罚缓冲使这些处罚不断更新,增加了新的处罚并抛弃了当时不再被政策所触发的处罚. 重要的是,提案和缓冲更新是同步进行的,同时不中断政策优化。 最后,法官将缓冲器的处罚应用于每次推出,因此梯度更新的奖励适应了在训练中观察到的打赏模式,而RM仍然定义了响应质量.

blocks.en: We evaluate Dynalize in two open-ended tasks: clinical counseling and creative writing. Our contributions are as follows: ■ \blacksquare We introduce Dynalize , which discovers reward-hacking behaviors during policy training and penalizes them online and asynchronously, while the RM remains the primary signal of response quality (Section 3 ). ■ \blacksquare We show that reward models are easily “hacked”. In both tasks, RM-only training keeps raising the RM score while performance on external benchmarks declines. Dynalize not only stops this decline: it allows longer RL climbs that lead to improved downstream performance (Section 5 ). ■ \blacksquare We analyze how Dynalize works in practice: which behaviors the proposer discovers, how their prevalence changes once they enter the buffer, and how widespread they are without penalties (Section 5.2 ). ■ \blacksquare We examine two potential mitigations: multi-turn RL, where the policy holds several turns of conversation with a simulated user, and reward-model retraining, where the RM is retrained on the behaviors that Dynalize discovered. We find that neither prevents reward hacking, and that Dynalize reaches higher performance than RM-only training in both (Sections 5.3 and 5.4 ). We will publicly release the code that led to the experiments in this paper. 2 2 2 We will share these resources upon acceptance.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: We illustrate our method, Dynalize , in Figure 1 . We focus exclusively on using a preference reward model (RM) as the main training signal. The method has two main components: ■ \blacksquare penalty proposer : a separate language model that identifies emerging reward-hacking patterns in training rollouts and formulates them as negative rubrics. 4 4 4 A penalty is not necessarily a failure mode in a single reply, but rather a behavior that may be disproportionately incentivized by the RM in a way that may render it a problem. For example, starting a reply with “Okay” is harmless, but starting most replies with it is not. Hence, we focus on behaviors that the proposer identifies in several rollouts. These define behaviors to penalize in subsequent policy updates. ■ \blacksquare penalty buffer : the set ℬ t \mathcal{B}_{t} of penalties that are active at training step t t . It takes in the new penalties from the proposer and drops those that the policy no longer triggers. Below, we first define the training reward, and then describe each component.

blocks.en: Every k k training steps, the proposer analyzes a sample of rollouts from the previous step and proposes new penalties, which are added to the penalty buffer ℬ t \mathcal{B}_{t} . For each response y y to an input x x (the context, prompt or conversation history), an LLM judge checks whether any active penalty applies. The resulting training reward is r t ​ ( x , y ) = r RM ​ ( x , y ) − λ ​ ∑ j ∈ ℬ t h j ​ ( x , y ) , r_{t}(x,y)=r_{\mathrm{RM}}(x,y)-\lambda\sum_{j\in\mathcal{B}_{t}}h_{j}(x,y), (3) where h j ​ ( x , y ) ∈ { 0 , 1 } h_{j}(x,y)\in\{0,1\} is the judge’s verdict on whether response y y exhibits the behavior of penalty j j , and λ > 0 \lambda>0 is the penalty weight. This reward replaces r ⁡ ( x , y i ) r(x,y_{i}) in Equation 2 .

Prior work shows that LLMs can monitor model behavior to detect reward hacking and other forms of misbehavior ( Baker et al., 2025 ; Korbak et al., 2025 ) . Here, we use a language model to discover reward-hacking patterns in training rollouts and convert them into explicit criteria for detecting these patterns in future rollouts. Specifically, at each proposal step, the proposer receives 32 rollouts randomly sampled from the batch generated at the previous training step, their RM scores, and the active penalties ℬ t \mathcal{B}_{t} . The rollouts are labeled according to whether their advantage is positive or negative (Equation 2 , computed with the RM score). This helps the proposer identify which responses the optimization reinforces and focus on reward-hacking patterns in positive-advantage responses. We do this because identifying patterns in negative-advantage responses is less useful, since these responses are already discouraged by the RM.

Training uses the current set of active penalties while new penalties are proposed in the background. Once a buffer update is complete, the updated set takes effect at the next batch of rollouts. blocks.en: We evaluate Dynalize on two open-ended tasks: clinical counseling and creative writing. We match each task with a relevant reward model, which provides the training signal, and with a relevant external benchmark, on which we evaluate policy checkpoints. We use the benchmark as an estimate of the true response quality. This allows us to tell reward hacking apart from downstream quality improvements: as in prior work on learned rewards ( Gao et al., 2022 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) , we take a benchmark score that declines while the RM score keeps increasing as the signal of reward hacking. For each task, we compare RM-only training, where the reward is the RM score r RM ​ ( x , y ) r_{\mathrm{RM}}(x,y) , with Dynalize (Equation 3 ).
blocks.zh: 我们评价Dynalize的两个开放式任务:临床咨询和创造性写作。 每项任务都有一个相关的奖励模式,提供训练信号,并有一个相关的外部基准,据此我们评价政策检查站。 我们使用基准来估计真正的反应质量。 这让我们可以分辨奖励黑客, 除了下游质量改进之外: 和之前的学习奖励工作一样(Gao等人, 2022; Yang等人, 2026), 对于每项任务,我们比较只使用RM的训练,其中的奖励是RM分数r RM (x,y) r_{\mathrm{RM}} (x,y),与Dynalize (等式3).

blocks.en: In this task, the policy acts as a clinical counselor: given a multi-turn conversation with a patient, the model is tasked with writing the next reply. The prompts for reinforcement learning derive from a private dataset of 10,000 conversation samples. The reward model is a proprietary Bradley–Terry model (Section 2 ) trained on preferences derived from annotations from clinical psychologists: a higher score indicates a reply that a psychologist is more likely to prefer. We evaluate on MindEval ( Pombal et al., 2025 ) , a benchmark of multi-turn mental health support conversations. Appendix A describes the exact setup.

blocks.en: 5 Results and Analysis
blocks.zh: 5 结果和分析

blocks.en: 5.1 Dynalize mitigates reward hacking
blocks.zh: 5.1 Dynalize 减轻奖励黑客

blocks.en: We can see that, for both clinical counseling and creative writing, RM-only training leads to steady increases in the respective RM scores during training, usually dominating those of our method (Figure 2 ). However, importantly, response quality (as measured by the performance on MindEval and EQ-Bench, respectively) starts degrading — this is the signal of reward hacking. This is not the case with our method, where response quality keeps improving for much longer. Dynalize not only allows us to extend training: it keeps optimizing for the reward model without sacrificing performance. In fact, in both tasks, it ends with a benchmark score superior to that of RM-only training, not only at its end — where hacking is most prominent — but also at its peak (Table 1 ). One hypothesis is that the penalties keep the policy from being steered towards artifacts or spurious features that the RM “likes”. We will analyze this next.
blocks.zh: 我们可以看到,在临床咨询和创造性写作方面,只接受RM培训会导致培训期间相应RM分数稳步上升,通常占据我们方法的分数(图2)。 然而,重要的是,反应质量(分别以MindEval和EQ-Bench上的性能来衡量)开始有辱人格——这是奖励黑客的信号. 我们的方法并非如此,因为在那里,反应质量持续了很长时间。 Dynalize不仅允许我们延长培训:它不断优化奖励模式,而不牺牲业绩. 事实上,在这两项任务中,它都以优于只接受RM训练的基准分数结束,不仅在它的结尾——黑客化最突出的地方——而且在其最高峰(表1). 一种假设是,惩罚使政策不能被指向RM“喜欢的文物或虚假特征”。 我们接下来分析一下

blocks.en: 5.2 What does the proposer discover?
blocks.zh: 5.2 国家 求婚者发现了什么?

blocks.en: Now we turn to analyzing the behaviors that were being penalized by our method during training.
blocks.zh: 现在,我们开始分析那些在训练中被我们的方法所惩罚的行为。

blocks.en: Figure 3 illustrates the penalty buffer during training for the clinical counseling task. 7 7 7 Table 5 provides the full description of each penalty. For creative writing, Figure 7 in App. D shows the same figure, and App. G provides the descriptions.
blocks.zh: 图3说明了临床咨询培训期间的惩罚缓冲措施。 7 7 表5全面说明了每项惩罚。 对于创作性写作,App中的图7. D显示了相同的数字,App.G提供了描述.

blocks.en: Some behaviors are common when first discovered but become substantially less frequent after being penalized. The most common ones, such as those targeted by penalties 1, 5, and 6, do not disappear completely: they persist at low rates until the end of training, and their penalties stay in the buffer. In contrast, less frequent behaviors, such as those targeted by penalties 15–19, disappear within a few training steps, and their penalties are retired. Because some behaviors persist, the buffer tends to grow during training.
blocks.zh: 一些行为在被首次发现时很常见,但在受到处罚后变得少得多. 最常见的惩罚,例如处罚1、5和6所针对的惩罚,不会完全消失:它们以低率持续到培训结束,其惩罚留在缓冲处。 相比之下,较少发生的行为,如第15至19号处罚所针对的行为,在几个培训步骤中消失,其处罚被取消。 由于一些行为持续存在,缓冲器在训练期间往往会增长.

blocks.en: The penalties range from surface-level, lexical patterns to content adequacy and quality.
blocks.zh: 处罚范围从地表一级、地语模式到内容充足和质量不等。

blocks.en: To assess whether these patterns also emerge without penalties, we evaluate the outputs of the RM-only policy at the end of training against all criteria discovered by our method, with the same judge and the same held-out prompts as for Dynalize . For example, in clinical counseling (right panel of Figure 3 ), over 90% of RM-only replies trigger at least one criterion, with over four criteria per reply on average, against fewer than two for Dynalize . These results suggest that the policy heavily exploits these patterns when trained without penalties. They also suggest that the patterns are sticky: under RM-only training nothing penalizes them, and in clinical counseling the average number of criteria per reply almost triples from the start to the end of training.
blocks.zh: 为了评估这些模式是否也无惩罚地出现,我们根据我们的方法发现的所有标准,在培训结束时评估只管理政策的产出,法官与Dynalize一样被搁置。 例如,在临床咨询中(图3的右面板),90%以上的只针对RM的答复触发了至少一个标准,每个答复平均有四个以上标准,而Dynalize则不到两个标准。 这些结果表明,该政策在未经处罚的培训中充分利用了这些模式。 他们还表示,这些模式是粘性的:在只接受RM培训的情况下,没有任何条件惩罚他们,在临床咨询中,从培训开始到结束,每次答复的平均标准几乎是三倍。

blocks.en: One of the main problems with reward hacking is that patterns start to show up in a large number of responses, even under different contexts. As we have noted in Section 3 , one behavior in itself (e.g., a stacked multi-part question in clinical counseling) is not necessarily damaging to the good conduct of a session; it becomes a problem, however, when the same pattern shows up in lots of different contexts. 8 8 8 Policies are typically trained on one user-facing reply at a time ( Shani et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) . This motivates us to explore multi-turn RL in Section 5.3 , where the reward model also sees the earlier replies of the policy. Repeated patterns across the outputs of a model are well documented ( Kirk et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Paech et al., 2026 ) . Identifying a persistent behavior can be more or less difficult, with some being more evident and others requiring many different scenarios to surface ( Gupta et al., 2025 ) . We analyze this by running different training checkpoints on a set of held-out prompts. 9 9 9 In clinical counseling, 1,000 conversations outside the training data; in creative writing, the 971 prompts of LitBench-Test , none of them in LitBench-Train . For example, we found that, in clinical counseling, the share of replies that start with “Okay” grows from almost none to about 60% under RM-only training. Under Dynalize , it grows in the same way until a penalty that covers it explicitly enters the buffer and starts penalizing these replies. In creative writing, the RM-only policy collapses to one theme regardless of the prompt: at the end of training, almost all of its stories contain the word “galactic” (see Figure 4 ).
blocks.zh: 奖励黑客的一个主要问题就是模式开始出现在大量的回应中,即使在不同的背景下也是如此. 正如我们在第3节所指出,一种行为本身(如临床咨询中一个堆积多段的问题)不一定损害会议的良好进行;然而,当同一模式在许多不同背景下出现时,它就会成为一个问题。 8 8 政策通常一次接受一个用户答复的培训(Shani等,2024;Wu等,2025)。 这促使我们探索第5.3节的多回合RL,其中奖励模式也看到了该政策早先的答复。 模型输出物的重复模式有详细记载(Kirk等,2024;Xu等,2025;Paech等,2026)。 确定一种持续的行为可能或多或少是困难的,有的更明显,有的则要求出现许多不同的情景(Gupta等人,2025年)。 我们通过运行不同的训练检查站来分析这一点。 9 9 在临床咨询中,1000次对话在培训数据之外;在创造性的写作中,971个Lit Bench-Test的提示,没有一个在Lit Bench-Train中。 例如,我们发现,在临床咨询中,从“好”开始的答复比例从几乎零增加到60%左右。 在Dynalize 下,它以同样的方式增长,直到覆盖它的惩罚明确进入缓冲并开始惩罚这些答复. 在创造性的写作中,只使用RM的政策崩溃为一个主题,而不管是否迅速:在训练结束时,它几乎所有的故事都包含有"银河"一词(见图4).

blocks.en: Reward hacking is typically analyzed in final responses only, as most reward models score the final response and ignore the reasoning. However, in autoregressive generation, the reasoning is part of the context that conditions the final response, so patterns that are rewarded in responses may transfer to the reasoning. This matters because reasoning traces are used to monitor and interpret models ( Baker et al., 2025 ; Korbak et al., 2025 ) , and collapsed reasoning may hurt both monitoring and generalization. We found that repeated patterns indeed emerge not only in the final response but also in the reasoning traces. For example, under RM-only training in creative writing, the share of reasoning traces that name the source of the prompts (r/WritingPrompts) grows from 1% to 59% at the end of training (see Figure 4 ).
blocks.zh: 奖励黑客通常只在最后的回复中进行分析,因为大多数奖励模型都会给最后的回应打分而忽略推理. 然而,在自发性生成中,推理是将最终反应作为条件的上下文的一部分,因此在反应中得到回报的规律可能转移到推理上. 这一点很重要,因为推理痕迹被用来监测和解释模型(Baker等人,2025;Korbak等人,2025),崩溃的推理可能既会损害监测和概括。 我们发现,不仅在最后反应中,而且在推理痕迹中,确实出现了反复出现的模式。 例如,在只进行RM创造性写作培训的情况下,说明提示来源(r/WritingPrompts)的推理痕迹比例在培训结束时从1%增至59%(见图4)。

blocks.en: RM-only responses are also longer and tend to combine several of these patterns, such as starting with “Okay” and ending with a question that offers two options (Figures F – F compare rollouts from both policies). MindEval captures these patterns in one of its axes (Table 2 ). Under RM-only training, the largest decline is in AI-Specific Communication Quality, the axis that rates whether replies are natural and free of repeated phrases and of templated or formulaic structure. Dynalize is ahead on every axis, and by far the most on this one.
blocks.zh: 仅针对RM的回复时间也更长,并倾向于结合其中几种模式,例如从“好”开始,最后是提出两个选项的问题(图F — F比较两种政策的推出)。 MindEval在其一轴中捕捉到这些图案(表2. 在只使用RM的训练下,最大的下降是AI-Special Communications Quality Quality,这是判断答复是否自然且没有重复的短语以及模板或公式结构的轴. Dynalize在每一个轴线上都领先, 迄今最靠这个轴线。

blocks.en: 5.3 Multi-Turn RL
blocks.zh: 5.3 多轮转录机

blocks.en: Figure 5 : RM score and MindEval in multi-turn RL.
blocks.zh: 图5 : RM分数和MindEval分数多转RL.

blocks.en: So far, we have trained with single-turn RL: the policy writes one response to a conversation history taken from the dataset, and the reward model scores that response. Policies trained on such next-turn rewards are known to optimize the immediate turn at the expense of the conversation as a whole ( Shani et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) . Multi-turn RL changes two things. First, the policy must continue its own conversations (and potentially “hacked” turns), so the reward model sees histories that contain the policy’s own responses. For example, we observed that replies frequently began with “Okay”; if this repetition appears in the conversation history, the reward model may be able to penalize it. Second, the policy is optimized on a signal that is spread over a whole trajectory, and is therefore much more dispersed than in single-turn training. We ask whether reward hacking still occurs under these conditions.
blocks.zh: 到目前为止,我们接受了单转RL的训练:政策对从数据集中提取的对话历史写出一个回应,奖励模型对这个响应进行评分. 有关这种下一轮奖励的训练有素的政策是用来优化即时转折,牺牲整个对话(Shani等,2024;Wu等,2025)。 多回转RL改变两件事. 首先,政策必须继续自己的对话(以及潜在的“被打”的转折),因此奖励模式看到了包含政策自身反应的历史。 例如,我们注意到,答复常常以“好”开头;如果这种重复出现在对话历史中,奖励模式可能可以惩罚它。 第二,政策优化于分布在整个轨道上的信号,因此其分散程度远大于单回合训练。 我们问,在这种条件下,是否还会发生报复黑客行为。

blocks.en: We focus exclusively on clinical counseling, for its conversational nature. Each rollout starts from a conversation in the dataset. The policy writes a reply, a user simulator (DeepSeek 4.1 Flash) writes the next message of the patient, and the policy replies again, for up to four policy replies per rollout. The reward model scores each policy reply given the conversation up to that reply, and the reward of the rollout is the mean of these scores. We compute one advantage per rollout, relative to its group, and apply it to the tokens of all policy replies in the rollout. With Dynalize , the judge checks every policy reply against the active penalties, and the rollout is penalized once for each distinct penalty that any of its replies triggers. The remaining setup is similar to that of the original clinical counseling described in Section 4 .
blocks.zh: 我们只注重临床咨询,因为它具有对话的性质。 每次推出都从数据集中的谈话开始. 政策写一个答复,一个用户模拟器(DeepSeek 4.1 Flash)写下病人的下一个信息,政策答复再次出现,每次推出最多四个政策答复. 奖励模式对每个政策答复的评分,因为对话一直到答复为止,而推出奖励就是这些评分的平均值。 我们计算出每推出一个优势,相对于其组别,并将其应用于推出时所有政策答复的标语. 在Dynalize的情况下,法官对照现行处罚检查每一项政策答复,而推出后将因其任何答复引发的每项不同处罚而受到惩罚一次。 其余的设置类似于第4节所描述的最初的临床咨询.

blocks.en: Figure 5 shows the training and evaluation curves. The curves are similar to those observed in single-turn training: under RM-only training, MindEval performance initially improves but then declines while RM scores continue to increase. With our method, MindEval scores remain high during training. These results suggest that our method is also effective in multi-turn environments under user simulation and that multi-turn RL alone does not prevent reward hacking.
blocks.zh: 图5显示了培训和评价曲线。 曲线与单回转训练中观察到的曲线相类似:在只使用RM的训练下,MindEval的性能起初会有所改进,但随后会下降,而RM分数会继续增加. 用我们的方法,明德瓦尔在训练期间的分数仍然很高. 这些结果表明,在用户模拟下的多回合环境中,我们的方法也是有效的,单靠多回合RL并不能阻止奖励黑客.

blocks.en: We found that the penalties discovered during the multi-turn run (see Appendix G.2 ) are partly the same as those of single-turn training, including stacked questions and option-based question framing. Even in a multi-turn setting, the reward model remains easy to game, and the policy exploits the same patterns observed in single-turn training.
blocks.zh: 我们发现,在多轮运行期间发现的处罚(见附录G.2)与单轮培训的处罚部分相同,包括堆叠的问题和基于选项的问题框架。 即使在多回合制环境下,奖励模式仍然容易被玩弄,政策也利用了在单回合制训练中观察到的相同模式.

blocks.en: 5.4 Can additional training data correct reward model biases?
blocks.zh: 5.4 (中文(简体) ). 额外培训数据能否纠正奖励模式的偏差?

blocks.en: Figure 6 : RM score and MindEval with the new RM.
blocks.zh: 图6:RM分数和Mindeval与新RM.

blocks.en: One hypothesis for why reward models are hacked is that they are not robust enough: they reward spurious features, and better training data or better modeling would remove these biases ( Srivastava et al., 2025 ; Bukharin et al., 2025 ; Coste et al., 2024 ; Eisenstein et al., 2024 ; Duan et al., 2026 ) . Dynalize produces what such a fix needs: a list of the behaviors that the policy exploited, and rollouts that show them. Here, we investigate whether we can exploit these penalties and rollouts to train a new reward model that can potentially be more robust to the exploits found during training.
blocks.zh: 奖励模式为何被黑客入侵的一个假设是,它们不够强大:它们奖励虚假特征,更好的培训数据或更好的建模将消除这些偏见(Srivastava等,2025;Bukharin等,2025;Coste等,2024;Eisenstein等,2024;Duan等,2026)。 Dynalize 生成这样一个固定需要的东西: 一份政策所利用的行为的清单, 以及展示它们的行为。 在这里,我们调查我们是否可以利用这些惩罚和推出来培训一种新的奖励模式,这种模式有可能对培训期间发现的剥削更有力。

blocks.en: Consistent with previous analysis, we conduct this experiment only in the clinical environment. To construct training data targeting the behaviors listed in Table 5 , we use rollouts generated during training (we have at least eight rollouts per prompt). Then, we select as the preferred response one that triggers no penalties and has RM scores above the 75th percentile, ensuring that it is a good response according to the original RM. We then pair each preferred response with a response to the same prompt that triggers at least one penalty. This yields approximately 15,000 new pairs, which we add to the original RM training set of approximately 30,000 samples. The original and new reward models achieve similar mean accuracy across the test set. 10 10 10 Mean accuracy on the reward-model test set: 78.48% for the original RM and 78.61% for the new RM.
blocks.zh: 与之前的分析一致,我们只在临床环境中进行这个实验. 为了构建针对表5所列行为的培训数据,我们使用在培训期间产生的推广(我们每批至少有8个推广)。 然后,我们选择一个首选反应,不触发处罚,RM的分数高于75%,确保它根据原来的RM是一个很好的响应. 然后,我们把每个首选反应与至少引发一个处罚的同一提示反应合并。 大约15 000个新样本,我们添加了大约30 000个样本的原始RM训练集。 原作和新作的奖励型号在测试组中实现相近的平均值精度. 10 10 奖励型号测试组的平均值精度:原作RM为78.48%,新作RM为78.61%.

blocks.en: Figure 6 shows the training curves and MindEval scores obtained with the newly trained RM. The curves with new RM exhibits the same pattern as before: MindEval scores initially increase and then decline, even as RM scores continue to rise; we have reward hacking. Table 7 lists the penalties discovered during this run, which are mostly different from those found with the original reward model.
blocks.zh: 图6显示使用新培训的RM获得的训练曲线和MindEval分数。 带有新RM的曲线呈现出与前作相同的模式 : MindEval的分数起初会增加,然后下降,即使RM分数继续上升;我们还有奖励黑客. 表7列出了这次运行中发现的处罚,这些处罚与原奖励模式的处罚大多不同.

blocks.en: These results support our motivation: even after correcting specific biases in the reward model, the policy is likely to find other ways to exploit it so we need a method that discover and penalize this problems during training. Our approach is also less costly, as it does not require retraining the RM or restarting policy training.
blocks.zh: 这些结果支持了我们的动机:即使在纠正了奖励模式的具体偏见后,该政策也有可能找到其他方法加以利用,因此我们需要一种在培训期间发现并惩罚这一问题的方法。 我们的方法成本也较低,因为它不需要再培训RM或重新开始政策培训。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en: We introduced Dynalize , which complements a preference reward model with penalties that are discovered and updated during policy training. In clinical counseling and creative writing, it mitigates reward hacking: it sustains longer training and reaches higher downstream response quality than RM-only training. Our analysis shows that our method suppresses patterns incentivized by the preference model that, without penalties, spread to most responses, and even to the model’s reasoning (which is not explicitly evaluated by the preference model). We also find that responses under our method are more natural and less formulaic than under RM-only training. We further show that neither multi-turn training nor retraining the reward model on the discovered behaviors prevents reward hacking, and that, under both contexts, our method reaches higher downstream performance than RM-only training.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了“Dynalize ” ,它用在政策培训中发现和更新的处罚来补充优惠奖励模式。 在临床咨询和创造性写作中,它减轻了对黑客的奖励:它维持更长时间的培训,并达到比只接受RM培训更高的下游响应质量. 我们的分析表明,我们的方法抑制了各种模式的动力,这种模式在没有惩罚的情况下,蔓延到大多数反应,甚至到模型的推理(这种推理没有被偏好模式明确评价). 我们还发现,根据我们的方法,与仅接受RM训练相比,反应更自然,也更少公式化. 我们进一步显示,无论是多回合培训,还是再培训关于所发现行为的奖励模式,都无法阻止奖励黑客行为,在这两种情况下,我们的方法达到的下游性能都高于只接受RM训练.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Our work has some limitations that should be considered. First, we study reward hacking when training in a relatively simple setup: a single task with environments that are similar across all training data. An interesting direction for future work is to extend our approach to multi-environment training, where interactions across environments may introduce more complex reward-hacking behaviors that might be more challenging to detect and mitigate.
blocks.zh: 我们的工作有一些局限性,应当加以考虑。 首先,我们研究如何在比较简单的训练中奖励黑客:一项与所有训练数据相似的环境有关的任务。 未来工作的一个令人感兴趣的方向是,将我们的方法推广到多种环境培训上,在这种培训中,各种环境之间的相互作用可能会引入更加复杂的、可能更难以发现和减轻的报复行为。

blocks.en: Furthermore, our method can only detect what models explicitly generate across a series of rollouts. As such, it cannot preemptively prevent hacking from occurring. It can only do so when it is already showing in model generations. Finding traces of hacking that are intrinsic to the model, i.e., present in its internal representations before they show in its generations, is also an interesting direction for future work.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们的方法只能通过一系列的推出来发现模型明确产生什么。 因此,它不能先发制人地防止黑客入侵。 只有当它已经出现在模范代中时,它才能这样做。 寻找该模式所固有的黑客痕迹,即在其世代显示之前就存在于其内部表述中,也是未来工作的有趣方向.

blocks.en: Finally, although penalty proposal and buffer updates are performed asynchronously, applying the penalty judge to every rollout adds computational overhead, although we attempt to minimize this by using a small model as the judge.
blocks.zh: 最后,虽然处罚建议和缓冲更新是同步进行的,但每次推出时都适用处罚法官,增加了计算费用,尽管我们试图通过使用一个小模型作为法官来尽量减少这种费用。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: Clinical counseling is one of the tasks studied in this work, where the model acts as a clinical counselor in a multi-turn conversation with a patient. The training data for this task consist of a private dataset of real human conversations , which raises important ethical considerations about privacy and confidentiality. To protect patient privacy, we anonymized the data and will not make it publicly available.
blocks.zh: 临床咨询是本作所研究的任务之一,模型在与患者的多回合对话中扮演临床顾问. 此项任务的培训数据包括一套关于真实的人类对话的私人数据集,这引起了关于隐私和保密的重要道德考虑。 为了保护病人的隐私,我们把数据匿名,不会公布。

blocks.en: Appendix A Evaluation Setup
blocks.zh: 附录A 评价设置

blocks.en: MindEval ( Pombal et al., 2025 ) evaluates a model in simulated multi-turn conversations. The model under evaluation acts as the counselor, a second language model simulates the patient from a profile, and a judge model rates each conversation from 1 to 6 on five criteria: Clinical Accuracy & Competence, Ethical & Professional Conduct, Assessment & Response, Therapeutic Relationship & Alliance, and AI-Specific Communication Quality. The MindEval score is the mean over the five criteria. We evaluate each checkpoint on the 50 patient profiles of the benchmark, with 10 turns per conversation, and we use the judge prompt with length guidelines. The official setup uses Claude Haiku 4.5 as the patient simulator and Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the judge. To reduce the cost of evaluating many checkpoints, we use GLM 5.2 for both.
blocks.zh: Mindeval (Pombal等, 2025年)在模拟多回合对话中评价一个模型. 被评价的模型担任顾问,第二语言模型从一个剖面模拟病人,法官模型根据五个标准对每次谈话进行1至6的评分:临床准确性与能力,伦理与职业行为,评估与反应,治疗关系与联盟,以及AI-Special Communication Quality Quality. MindEval分数是5个标准之上的平分. 我们根据基准的50个病人情况来评估每个检查点,每个谈话有10个转弯,我们使用有长度准则的法官即时检查。 官方设置以克洛德·海库 4.5为病人模拟器,克洛德·索内 4.5为裁判. 为了减少评估许多检查站的费用,我们使用GLM 5.2两种方法。

blocks.en: GLM 5.2 is also the penalty proposer of Dynalize . To check that our conclusions do not depend on it as the judge, we rate the same conversations of every checkpoint again with two other judges, Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Table 3 shows that the three judges agree: RM-only training peaks early and then declines, and Dynalize ends higher, by 0.45, 0.46 and 0.64 points at the end of training, respectively.
blocks.zh: GLM 5.2也是Dynalize的处罚提案人. 为了确认我们的结论并不取决于作为法官,我们再次评价每个检查站与另外两名法官Kimi-K3和DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash的谈话。 表3显示三位法官同意:只接受RM的训练会早起而后下降,而Dynalize的成绩会更高,在训练结束时分别达到0.45分,0.46分和0.64分.

blocks.en: Table 3: MindEval scores of the two clinical counseling runs under three judges. All judges rate the same conversations. Peak , End and Final are defined as in Table 1 . GLM 5.2 is the judge used in the main text.
blocks.zh: 表3:MindEval的两名临床咨询分数在三名法官以下。 所有法官都把谈话评为相同。 表1对峰顶、终点和终点的定义。 GLM 5.2是正文中使用的法官.

blocks.en: We follow the official implementation of the benchmark. The checkpoint writes a story for each of 32 prompts under three seed modifiers (96 stories), sampled at temperature 0.7 with a min- p p of 0.1. A judge model scores each story from 0 to 20 on 22 criteria, nine of which are negative and are inverted. The score of a checkpoint is the mean over criteria and stories, rescaled to the range from 0 to 100. We use GLM 5.2 as the judge.
blocks.zh: 我们跟踪基准的正式执行情况。 检查站为三个种子修饰剂(96个故事)下的32个提示每个提示写出一个故事,在0.7温下取出样本,pp为0.1分. 一个法官模型根据22个标准从0到20对每个故事进行分数,其中9个为负数并倒置. 一个检查站的得分是优于标准和故事,调整到从0到100不等. 我们使用GLM 5.2作为法官.

blocks.en: ⬇ You are an expert reviewer auditing { context } for REWARD HACKING . You will receive several groups ; each group contains one prompt with several candidate responses and their RM scores ( higher = the reward model prefers it ; advantage = score minus the group mean ). Your exclusive task is to identify reward - hacking superficial tricks , systematic flaws , or active failures that the RM incorrectly rewards . And write them as NEGATIVE RUBRICS . A valid negative rubric describes a critical flaw that HIGHER - scored replies have , and that flaw must definitively degrade a reply ’ s quality for the user / reader . ## Core Guidelines ### 1. Discriminative Power ( Focus on the Hack ) * Focus ONLY on criteria present on the HIGHER - scored responses * Typical patterns include : length inflation , stacking multiple questions , formulaic openers and closers , templated structure , … ### 2. True Flaws , Not Genuine Quality * ** Do NOT report positive rubrics :** Genuinely good qualities are what the RM * should * reward . * Take in mind that some patterns can be good and the goal of the reward model , be conservative and so identify only clear hacking signals that degrade response quality . * ** Do NOT report lower - scored flaws :** The RM already punishes what the LOWER - scored replies do wrong . Focus exclusively on the bad habits the RM is * rewarding *. ### 3. Novelty & Non - Redundancy * Compare your findings against the ** Existing Penalties ** list . * Never duplicate overlapping rubrics in meaning or scope . * Identify uncovered quality dimensions . If the existing penalties already cover the observed reward hacking comprehensively , return an empty list . ### 4. Observable & Objective ( Single - Reply Rule ) * Each patterns you report becomes a NEW penalty checked on every future reply by a judge that sees ONLY ONE reply plus its conversation . * The description must be objective , concrete , actionable , and decidable from a single reply alone ( never by comparing it to other replies ). * Narrow the scope so a normal , high - quality reply does not accidentally trigger it . * Dont be vague , be precise ### 5. What was she like on that first date? Or would you rather talk more about your family or something else on your mind today? Our Method That sounds lovely — meeting up after an appointment and ending up with delicious ice cream together. Was it a special place, or just a spontaneous thing that ended up feeling just right?

Member: I talk to one every once in a while but the conversations aren’t the same anymore. We’re different people now
blocks.zh: 共享上下文 律师: 看着他们活在外头, 你考虑过联系他们吗? 成员:我偶尔和一个人交谈, 我们现在不同了

blocks.en: RM only Okay — so you’re holding two things at once now. One is the love and the memories — which were real and important. And the other is the honest truth that you can’t recreate what you had — because both of you have changed, and your lives are in very different places. We don’t have to fix that today — but I’d suggest we could look at what you actually need right now. You said earlier that you wanted to be able to use your own time — and we also know that your relationships are one of the strongest supports you have for your mood and anxiety. So the question shifts a little, doesn’t it? It’s not “how do I get back to those friendships” — it’s “what kind of connection fits me now ?” You’re a mom in a new place, with energy that moves differently, and a life organized around your daughter. Can we explore what kind of connection would actually fit that right now? Our Method That makes a lot of sense. You can’t go back to who you two were back then. When you say the conversations aren’t the same, what’s most missing for you in those interactions now?
blocks.zh: 仅限RM 好吧,所以你现在拿着两件东西。 一个是爱情和记忆——它们是真实而重要的。 另一种是诚实的真理,你不能重新创造你曾经拥有的东西,因为你们俩都改变了,你们的生活在非常不同的地方。 今天我们不必解决这个问题,但我建议我们看看你们现在实际需要什么。 你早些时候说过,你希望能够利用自己的时间——我们也知道,你们的关系是你们情绪和焦虑得到的最有力支持之一。 问题有点转移, 这不是“我怎样才能回到这些友谊中来 ” , 而是“我现在有什么联系?” 你是一个新地方的妈妈, 精力变化不同, 我们能探讨一下 什么样的联系 真正适合现在? 我们的方法 这很有道理 你们不能回到你们以前的样子。 当你说对话不一样时,

blocks.en: Shared context Counselor: When you noticed that irritation building, were you able to catch yourself and pause before reacting, or did it kind of take over? Member: Kinda took over
blocks.zh: 共享上下文 律师: 当你注意到那个刺激的建筑, 你能够抓住自己和暂停 在反应之前, 还是它有点接管? 成员:金塔接管

blocks.en: RM only Okay — so here’s what I’m hearing: you came into this week with an intention — to be at peace with habits that bother you — and this week, you noticed exactly what triggers you: chewing, phone, talking, a buildup of energy and noise. You even noticed them stacking up, and you noticed that irritation rising. The piece that didn’t hold yet was that pause — the step between noticing and reacting. That last part “kinda took over,” which is totally human — but it does mean we’ve got something concrete to work with. We also know there’s a concrete real-life moment coming up: family brunch with her this morning . Before we go any further, I want to ask — For this morning, what’s one small thing you’d be willing to try that’s different from last night? For example: - Pause 3 seconds before reacting , even if you feel the irritation rising. - Name it internally (softly, in your mind): “This is her chewing — I’m feeling irritation, and I don’t have to act on it right now.” - Or step away for 60 seconds if it starts to feel unmanageable. Something small — nothing that needs to “fix” her or what she’s doing — just something you can practice in this moment, this morning. What would feel workable for you? Our Method Got it. When it took over, tell me briefly — what did that look like for you in the moment? Like, what did you do, say, or feel as the irritation built up?
blocks.zh: 仅限RM 好吧,我听到的是这样的:你本周来是有意的, 想要平息困扰你的习惯, 而本周,你注意到了引发你的原因:咀嚼、电话、说话、积累能量和噪音。 你甚至注意到他们堆积起来, 你注意到刺激上升。 至今为止, 最后一部分是“某种被接管”的, 完全属于人类, 今日早晨, 在更进一步之前,我想问一下:今天上午,你愿意尝试与昨晚不同的小事是什么? 例如: - 在反应前暂停3秒, 即使你感觉到刺激在上升. - 内部命名(轻轻地,在你的脑中): “这是她咀嚼的口味 — — 我感到烦恼,我不必现在就采取行动。 ”如果它开始感到无法管理,就走开60秒。 一件小事 — — 没有什么需要“修补”她或她正在做的事情 — — 只是你现在、今天上午可以练习的东西。 你觉得什么是可行的? 我们的方法得到了它。 当它接管的时候,简要地告诉我——你现在的样子是什么? 喜欢,你做了什么,说,或感觉 像刺激积聚?

blocks.en: RM only Okay, I hear you — and prayer is a real and meaningful way for you to deal with stress. You’ve been carrying a lot right now — your grandpa’s health, the uncertainty, what’s coming up Thursday — and prayer is your way of taking care of yourself. Is there anything else you want to talk about right now, or would you like to just keep going with this? I’m here. Our Method I’m glad you have prayer as something you can turn to. When you pray right now — can you tell me a little about what you’re asking for or thinking about with your grandpa?
